body.cap: Yujin Choi, Manager at NP, delivers a presentation at the Global Media Meetup with Ubergizmo held at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 3 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: NP Inc. (Co-CEOs Seung-Up Baek and Ji-Hoon Choi) participated in the Global Media Meetup for Korean startups on September 3.

The Global Media Meetup, co-hosted by AVING News and U.S. tech media Ubergizmo, focused on introducing the products and technologies of Korean companies and startups to the global market. It also aimed to provide early media exposure and business opportunities for CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and CES participants.

NP, founded in 2006 as an event specialist under the vision of “limitless experiences that deliver better life value to humanity,” has successfully executed major events such as the opening and closing ceremonies of the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics, the 20th Presidential Inauguration, and Seoul Light at DDP.

After proving its strength in large-scale offline event planning and execution, the company established ‘NP XR-Stage,’ a dedicated XR virtual production studio. Expanding into entertainment, broadcasting, film, drama, and e-commerce content production, NP became the first in its industry to achieve a KOSDAQ listing in 2021.

Recently, NP has expanded into the emerging personalized XR HMD (head-mounted display) market. Leading this new business is its emotion-recognition-based XR meditation solution, ‘MUA,’ which will attract global attention at CES 2026.

body.cap: Promotional image of MUA | Image by NP

body.x: MUA aims to create new opportunities in the wellness industry. It designs visual elements inspired by nature—such as clouds, lakes, and caves—and combines them with hyper-realistic 3D backgrounds to create immersive virtual environments. This helps users achieve deeper meditative states more quickly.

Beyond multisensory meditation content, MUA applies algorithms that maximize meditation experiences by analyzing biosignals. In collaboration with KAIST’s Department of Brain & Cognitive Sciences and the Meditation Science Institute, NP developed emotion inference algorithms based on biosignals, currently undergoing validation.

Biosignals are collected through MUA’s dedicated app installed on HMDs, smartphones, and wearables. Indicators such as age, gender, heart rate, heart rate variability, oxygen saturation, and sleep quality are analyzed to determine psychological and emotional conditions. Based on this, MUA delivers meditation content tailored to the user’s real-time needs, a key differentiator.

Collected biosignal data is analyzed using James Russell’s two-dimensional emotion model, which quantifies valence, arousal, and stress on scales of 1 to 10. These are then mapped onto 16 emotion states. During the first five sessions, user feedback fine-tunes discrepancies between subjective perception and algorithmic inference.

body.cap: Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo, experiences NP’s XR meditation app MUA at the Global Media Meetup | Photo by AVING News

body.x: As users continue sessions, MUA’s AI model incorporates real-time data, accumulated usage history, and feedback to create individualized base models through reinforcement learning. This reduces emotion inference errors over time.
Most importantly, by delivering meditation content optimized to personal psychological and physiological conditions, MUA dramatically shortens the long learning curve of traditional meditation.

For example, traditional MBSR (Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction) meditation requires daily practice of at least 10 minutes for eight weeks to reach deep immersion. MUA, however, enables users to get focused states within just 3–5 minutes through audiovisual guidance and interactive elements.

MUA’s UX·UI prioritizes emotional stability with principles of balance, minimalism, psychological accessibility, and emotional-sensory touch. Its central logo graphic reinforces stability, while simple circular gestures allow easy control of all functions. Even users unfamiliar with HMDs can focus solely on meditation without difficulty.

body.cap: Illustration of MUA’s user interface | Image by NP

body.x: Manager Yujin Choi explained, “By minimizing complex buttons and animations, we reduce unnecessary stimulation and create a calm atmosphere through visual spacing. The content transitions smoothly between MR and VR environments to minimize motion sickness. All meditation sessions flow from reality into virtual space and back, guiding users into deep immersion.”
Mindfulness has become a significant trend in advanced economies, driving growing interest in meditation apps.
In 2024, global meditation apps like Calm, Headspace, and Insight Timer recorded an estimated 230–250 million cumulative downloads, with 70–80 million monthly active users.

According to Verified Market Reports, the global meditation app market is projected to grow from USD 4.2 billion in 2024 to USD 12.1 billion by 2033, with a CAGR of 12.9% from 2026 to 2033. Expanding device accessibility and workplace wellness programs are fueling opportunities. With immersive XR environments and data-driven optimization algorithms, MUA is expected to gain unique recognition.

body.cap: NP officials pose with Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo, during the Global Media Meetup at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 3 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: NP launched MUA’s beta version in March and has since attracted users in over 20 countries. The company plans to target the North American market in earnest at CES 2026. The U.S. has the world’s highest HMD household penetration rate, at 15–17%.

Choi said, “CES is the optimal opportunity to rapidly boost recognition of our company and service in North America. With clear industry growth and social demand, MUA will set a new standard for technology-driven meditation and secure a unique position.”

He added, “NP will advance MUA’s biosignal-based emotion diagnostics and personalized meditation recommendation technology to evolve into a digital therapeutic. By challenging for a CES Innovation Award, we aim to share our vision globally, validate the reliability of our technology on the world stage, seek collaboration with experts, and accelerate clinical and therapeutic research to build a platform that erases the boundary between wellness and therapy.”

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo runs Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries, focusing on electronics and technology. It covers major exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen, a former NVIDIA programming engineer and 3D graphics developer, attended the event and has reported annually from CES on global companies’ products and technologies.
